name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Femur

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Femur

criteria.description: Presence of congenital nonunion or pseudoarthrosis of the femoral diaphysis
Radiographic evidence of cystic and sclerotic changes at the pseudoarthrosis site
Presence or history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) or café-au-lait spots
Clinical deformity of the thigh with limb shortening and abnormal mobility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital femoral pseudoarthrosis with radiographic confirmation; supportive findings such as NF1 features increase diagnostic confidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing for NF1 mutations may aid in associated cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital femoral pseudoarthrosis with pathological fracture
searchTerms: birth defect causing false joint in thigh bone
broken thigh bone that doesn't heal

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiographic cystic and sclerotic changes at femoral diaphysis
searchTerms: x-ray showing cysts and hard spots in thigh bone
bone changes with holes and dense areas
femur shaft with mixed cystic and sclerotic lesions

common.symptomName: Progressive anterolateral bowing of the femur
searchTerms: thigh bone bending forward and to the side

common.symptomName: Limb length discrepancy due to femoral shortening
searchTerms: one leg shorter due to thigh bone
unequal leg length from femur shortening

common.symptomName: Abnormal mobility or instability at the pseudoarthrosis site
searchTerms: unstable false joint in thigh bone
abnormal movement at bone nonunion site

common.symptomName: Pain localized to the affected thigh
searchTerms: pain in the affected thigh region

occasional.symptomName: Neurofibromas or other neurofibromatosis type 1 manifestations
searchTerms: soft skin lumps from nerve growths

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy of the affected thigh
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in upper leg

rare.symptomName: Pathological fractures in other long bones
Joint stiffness adjacent to the pseudoarthrosis
searchTerms: limited joint movement next to pseudoarthrosis

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to NF1 plexiform neurofibromas
searchTerms: neurological symptoms due to plexiform neurofibromas

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; genetic testing may reveal NF1 mutations
imaging: X-ray showing femoral diaphyseal nonunion with cystic and sclerotic changes
MRI may demonstrate soft tissue involvement and exclude other pathologies
genetic: Mutations in NF1 gene in cases associated with neurofibromatosis type 1
other: Clinical examination revealing abnormal mobility and limb deformity

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized bone fragility with multiple fractures
Radiographic ground-glass appearance of bone lesions
History of trauma preceding fracture nonunion
Radiographic evidence of fracture healing attempts

redFlags: Pathological fracture with minimal or no trauma
Progressive limb deformity and shortening in infancy
Failure of fracture healing despite appropriate treatment
references: Joseph B, et al. Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the femur: a review of pathogenesis and management. J Pediatr Orthop. 2019.
